caseno:
First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 99 of 2019.
(Civil Rule No. 135 (FM) of 2016)
lawyer:
Syeda Shawkat Ara, Advocate—For the Appellant-petitioner. 
Sikder Mahmudur Razi with Md Zahirul Islam, Advocates—For the Respondent-Opposite-Party No. 1.
parties:
Jamil Ahmed (Md) -------- Appellant
VS
Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation and others -------- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. This appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 30-7-2015 passed by the learned District Judge, Khulna in Title Execution Case No. 21 of 2012 rejecting an application so filed by the present appellant dated 30-7-2015 praying for providing him installment to pay the decretal dues to the respondent-bank by giving him 5-7 years time. 

 The present respondent No. 1 as petitioner originally filed a case being Miscellaneous Case No. 25 of 1997 under Article 27 of Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation Order, 1973 (Presidential Order (PO) No. 7 of 1973) against the present appellant and another making them as opposite-parties stating inter alia that, by mortgaging the scheduled property, by a registered deed bearing No. 2035, the predecessor of the present appellant and respondent nos. 2-11 availed a loan amounting to Taka 7,60,000 on 4-2-1985 with the commitment that, he would repay an amount of Taka 5,521/35 as monthly installment payable in 30 years. But after availing that loan, the loanee has failed to pay any installment for which the respondent No. 1 on 23-7-1996 issued a legal notice asking the loanee to pay the loan stood at Taka 17,17,448/23 on 30-9-1996 but as the loanee did not come forward to pay the said amount hence the case. 

 4. In the said Miscellaneous Case, the present appellant and another as opposite-party nos. 1 and 2 contested the case by filing two separate sets of written objection alleging inter alia that, the respondent-bank did not claim the amount calculating the same imposing simple interest rather in a very slipshod manner higher interest was added with the claim for which they did not repay the loan amount in time. It has further been alleged that, since the loan was for a certain tenure so before expiry of that very tenure, the bank is not entitled to claim the amount and hence, the said Miscellaneous Case is liable to be dismissed. 

 5. The learned District Judge, Khulna in order to dispose of the said case framed a single issue and after considering the material and evidence on record, he vide judgment and order dated 9-3-1998 allowed the Miscellaneous Case for an amount of Taka 17,17,448/23 as of 15-4-1998 directing the opposite-parties to the case to pay the claim amount with interest within 15-4-1998 in default, it has further been ordered to sell the mortgaged property to realize the decretal amount. As the appellant-opposite-parties to the Miscellaneous Case did not come forward to repay the decretal dues, the respondent No. 1-bank then on 8-3-1999 filed an execution case being Title Execution Case No. 28 of 1999 claiming the decretal amount of Taka 17,17,448/23. 

 6. When the said execution case was proceeding, the appellant-judgment-debtor on 30-7-2015 filed an application seeking installment to repay the decretal amount on making payment of Taka 2,80,000 and prayed for re-schedulement of the loan in line with the circular being circulation No. 002-2008. The said application was taken up for hearing by the learned District Judge and vide impugned order dated 30-7-2015 rejected the same holding that, the he has got no authority to provide 5-7 years in paying the decretal amount by giving installment. 

 7. It is at that stage, one of the judgment-debtors as appellant came before this court by filing this appeal. After filing the appeal, the self-same appellant also filed an application for stay of the operation of the impugned judgment and this court vide order dated 9-3-2016 issued rule and stayed the further proceedings of the said Title Execution Case No. 28 of 1999 for a period 6(six) months with a condition to pay Taka 15,000 per months. The said order then gave rise to Civil Rule No. 135 (FM) of 2016. 

 9. The learned counsel by filing a supplementary-affidavit and by annexing the receipts showing payment of installment at Taka 15,000 from the date, the rule was issued further submits that, from the date of direction, the bank is not entitled to add any interest upon the decretal amount so claimed in the execution case. With those two submissions, the learned counsel finally prays for allowing the appeal as well as making the rule absolute. 

 10. On the contrary, Mr Sikder Mahmudur Razi, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent-opposite-party No. 1 by filing a counter-affidavit as well as supplementary counter-affidavit annexing relevant documents at the very outset submits that, under the provision of Article 26 of PO No. 7 of 1973, there has been no scope on the part of the creditor herein respondent No. 1 to wait for the entire tenure to claim the outstanding loan and thus the respondent-bank has rightly initiated the Miscellaneous Case as it is admitted position that the appellant did not pay single installment till filing of the Miscellaneous Case and there has been no illegality in the impugned order rejecting the application of the appellant praying for installment. 

 12. The learned counsel next contends that, since in the year 1986, the loan was disbursed and in the year 1997 that is, more than 11 years of disbursing the loan, the Miscellaneous Case was filed and during that long period of time not a single monthly installment was paid by the borrower so there has been no scope on the part of the bank but to initiate a Miscellaneous Case to realize the unpaid amount. 

 13. The learned counsel further submits that, since after passing the contesting decree against the appellant, he even come forward to pay the amount so the respondent-bank has rightly initiated the Title Execution Case to realize the amount and when there has been no scope to give installment and therefore, the impugned order has rightly been passed which calls for no interference by this Hon'ble court and finally prays for dismissing the appeal and that of discharging the rule. 

 15. There has been no gainsaying the fact that, the Miscellaneous Case initiated under Article 27 was contesting one. So the appellant-petitioner has every knowledge about the said decree yet he did not come forward to pay the decretal amount. It is at the fag-end of the execution case when the bank was going to sale the mortgaged property through auction by publishing auction notice, the appellant-petitioner then entered appearance in the execution case and filed the application which clearly shows the utter negligence of the appellant-petitioner to repay the decretal amount. 

 16. Now question remains, whether the amount so paid by the appellant after passing the direction by this court will be deducted from the amount which stood on the date of filing the execution case or not.
